The AQA 8203 specification page links one shared PDF covering 8201-8206. I pulled it from AQA's CDN and read it directly. Cover page, verbatim: "Version 1.2 1 February 2026". The claimed version number and issue date are CORRECT.

THE DIFF IS REAL AND MATERIAL. I compared the live v1.2 against our archived baseline (specs/aqa/art-and-design-8203-8203.md, "Version 1.0 23 October 2015").
Section 2.2, Component 1 "What's assessed":
- v1.0: "It must include a sustained project ... AND A SELECTION OF FURTHER WORK undertaken during the student's course of study."
- v1.2: "It must include a sustained project evidencing the journey from initial engagement to the realisation of intentions." The clause is deleted.
Section 2.3.1, Component 1 details:
- v1.0: "The portfolio must include BOTH: 1. A sustained project ... 2. A SELECTION OF FURTHER WORK resulting from activities such as trials and experiments; skills-based workshops; mini and/or foundation projects; responses to gallery, museum or site visits; work placements; independent study..."
- v1.2: "The portfolio must include a sustained project developed in response to a subject, theme, task or brief..." The "both:" construction and numbered item 2 are deleted entirely.
The live HTML "specification at a glance" page independently corroborates: portfolio = sustained project only.

This is NOT admin-only. It deletes a mandatory minimum content requirement from a component worth 60% of the GCSE. Weightings are unchanged (Component 1 still 96 marks / 60%; Component 2 still 96 marks / 40%), so the change is to required NEA content, not structure — but it is still material for teaching and portfolio planning.

REFUTATION ROUTES ATTEMPTED, ALL FAILED
1. "Does not exist" — refuted; v1.2 cover and body wording read directly from the live PDF.
2. "Different board/spec" — refuted; the PDF is AQA and explicitly covers 8201-8206, so Graphic communication (8203) is in scope. Note the same change therefore hits all six titles (8201, 8202, 8203, 8204, 8205, 8206), not just 8203.
3. "Applies to A-level, not GCSE" — this was the strongest lead, because our stored record warns that an AQA Art & Design ESA confidentiality update (new 1 February pre-release) applies to A-level only. That warning is valid for the ESA change but does NOT explain this one. The portfolio wording change is in the GCSE specification document itself.
4. "Withdrawn / different cohort" — refuted; AQA key dates show a June 2027 series with entry codes 8203/C and 8203/X and an NEA deadline of 31 May 2027. No discontinuation notice.
5. "Stale CMS metadata proves it is still v1.0" — the AQA page's embedded Sanity metadata still reads versionNumber "1.0", dated 23/10/2015. That field is stale and is contradicted by the actual PDF it serves. Not a valid refutation, but it explains how a checker could wrongly conclude "no change".

"Effective for the 2027 cohort, first assessment summer 2027" is a reasonable inference, not an AQA statement. The v1.2 PDF has no changelog or amendment table, and I found no cohort-effective notice on the 8203 pages. The cover still reads "For teaching from September 2016 onwards / For GCSE exams in 2018 onwards". Publication on 1 Feb 2026 falls after the summer-2026 cohort's portfolios were effectively complete, so summer 2027 is the first series taught wholly under v1.2. Treat the 2027 attribution as sound but inferred.

SCOPE. The article says: "an important update to our GCSE Art & Design (8201-8206) qualification that will apply from first assessment in summer 2027". The 8201-8206 family includes Photography 8206. The claim's scope is correct.

CONTENT. The article says: "From 2027 onwards, Component 1 will consist of a minimum requirement of one sustained project only and the requirement for further work will be removed." The claim quotes this correctly.

INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION IN THE SPEC. I downloaded the live specification PDF. It reads "GCSE ART AND DESIGN (8201, 8202, 8203, 8204, 8205, 8206) ... Version 1.2, 1 February 2026". The phrase "further work" occurs ZERO times in the whole document. Component 1 now reads: "The portfolio must include a sustained project developed in response to a subject, theme, task or brief". The HTML spec pages (specification-at-a-glance, scheme-of-assessment) match, with zero hits for "further work". The change is real and is already published.

REFUTATION ROUTES TESTED AND CLOSED:
1. "Does not exist" — REFUTED. The AQA news URL returns HTTP 200 with the exact title.
2. "Different board or family" — REFUTED. The article names 8201-8206 explicitly; 8206 Photography is section 3.9 of the same document.
3. "Different cohort" — REFUTED. The article states "first assessment in summer 2027", which is exactly the 2027 cohort.
4. "Predates our build" — NOT APPLICABLE, but for a different reason than the audit rule assumes: the change is recent (2026), not old.
5. "Admin-only" — PARTLY TRUE BUT NOT ENOUGH. It changes a minimum assessment requirement inside Component 1, which is 60% of the qualification. That is more than administration.
6. "Withdrawal" — NOT CLAIMED and NOT TRUE. See below.

STILL OFFERED IN 2027: YES. The AQA key dates page for 8206 lists a 31 May 2027 non-exam assessment submission deadline for both 8206/C and 8206/X in the June 2027 series. The page has zero occurrences of "withdraw", "final assessment" or "last exams". The specification header still reads "For teaching from September 2016 onwards / For GCSE exams in 2018 onwards". Therefore confirmed_withdrawn = false and still_offered_2027 = true.

MITIGATION — WHY THE PRACTICAL RISK IS LOW. Although the claim survives, three facts limit its effect on our build ledger:
(a) The change is PERMISSIVE, not restrictive. AQA states learners "can still choose to produce further work if they wish, and it will still be assessed in the normal way". A centre that keeps its old portfolio structure stays compliant.
(b) There is NO subject-content change. AQA confirms no change to the Assessment Objectives, no change to the weighting of Component 1, no change to the assessment criteria balance of marks, and no change to the expected breadth and depth. AO1-AO4 each stay at 25%.

The adversarial attempt to refute the withdrawal failed. The first-pass RED verdict is upheld.

PRIMARY EVIDENCE (board's own site). The WJEC qualification page for GCSE Art and Design carries a phase-out notice, quoted verbatim: "Summer 2026 will be the final full assessment opportunity for this qualification. A resit opportunity for Unit 2 will be available in January 2027, subject to demand." The page identifies the qualification as spec code 3650QS (Art, Craft and Design), Ofqual QN 601/8251/9, QWADN code C00/0780/4 - an exact match to the audited target. WJEC has a separate live page, "GCSE Art and Design - Teaching from 2025", carrying a new endorsed-title suite with new spec codes: 3610QS (Art, Craft and Design), 3611QS (Fine Art), 3612QS (Textile Design), 3613QS (Graphic Communication), 3614QS (Three-Dimensional Design), 3615QS (Photography). It shows "Teaching: Sept 2025". This is the made-for-Wales replacement. First teaching September 2025 on a two-year GCSE gives a first award of summer 2027 - which is precisely why the legacy 3650QS suite has no summer 2027 series. This is a full replacement, not an amendment, so the new codes are a different qualification requiring a fresh build.

WHY 2027 IS NOT AVAILABLE. The only 2027 opportunity WJEC offers on 3650QS is a January 2027 Unit 2 resit, and even that is conditional ("subject to demand"). A single conditional unit resit is not a full assessment opportunity and is not a summer 2027 series. Any Year 10 starting September 2025 - i.e. the 2027 cohort - is barred by WJEC from entry onto 3650QS entirely. There is no route by which a 2027 candidate sits this specification.

REGISTER CHECKS (attempted, inconclusive - not contradicting). I could not read the Ofqual register. register.ofqual.gov.uk now 301-redirects to find-a-qualification.services.ofqual.gov.uk, and every search and detail URL pattern I tried on the new service returned its "Page not found" page; the legacy path bounces on to gov.uk. I also tried the Qualifications Wales QiW database (qiw.wales) by approval number C00/0780/4 and by keyword search - all 404. Note that 3650QS is a Wales-only qualification regulated by Qualifications Wales, so QiW rather than Ofqual is its true home register. These register failures are tooling/URL failures, not evidence of continued availability: nothing on either register contradicted the WJEC notice. The stated bar for confirmed_withdrawn is an explicit final-assessment date "on the board's own site OR Ofqual", and the board's own site meets it unambiguously.

TOOL LIMITATION. The session's WebSearch budget (200/200) was exhausted before I started, so all work was done with direct WebFetch against known authoritative hosts rather than search. This did not affect the outcome - the decisive evidence sits on the WJEC page itself.

VERDICT. amendment_summary: WJEC ran a survey (1-17 October 2025, 438 respondents from 60% of Welsh schools) and chose "Option 1". WJEC amends Unit 3 (the practical assessment unit) only. Units 1 and 2 stay unchanged. The new Unit 3 aligns with Unit 7: Scientific Enquiry of the new GCSE The Sciences (Double Award). The amended Unit 3 applies to Year 10 cohorts that start in September 2026, so its first assessment is summer 2028. The summer 2027 cohort (started September 2025) keeps the existing Unit 3. Separate GCSE Biology, Chemistry and Physics are RETAINED in Wales and continue until summer 2031. The new GCSE The Sciences (Double Award) replaces the legacy Science (Double Award) only, not the separate sciences; its first teaching moved to September 2026. Qualifications Wales will consult in autumn 2028 on the science suite that follows summer 2031.
action: BUILD-READY, but pick the correct Unit 3 version first. No withdrawal risk: WJEC confirms the separate sciences continue to summer 2031, and the new Double Award does not replace them. The qualification is fully valid for summer 2027. The AMBER flag is a build-timing caveat, not a health warning. Because first teaching of the amended Unit 3 starts this September, a build now serves two different Unit 3 populations at once: Year 11 in 2026/27 (exams summer 2027) sit the ORIGINAL Unit 3; Year 10 from September 2026 (exams summer 2028) sit the AMENDED Unit 3. Recommended build order: build Units 1 and 2 now without reservation, because they are unchanged and stay valid to summer 2031 (that is roughly 90% of the content). Then download the amended specification from the WJEC Biology page and build Unit 3 against the NEW scientific-enquiry approach, since every cohort from September 2026 onward uses it and the original Unit 3 has only one exam series left. If you want full 2027 coverage, hold a short legacy Unit 3 variant for one year, then retire it. One gap in the audit: the Ofqual register has migrated to find-a-qualification.services.ofqual.gov.uk and blocked direct record fetches, and the QiW search is client-side rendered, so no regulator end-date field was read. The evidence is nonetheless strong, because it comes from WJEC's own qualification pages and WJEC's published decision article, corroborated by Qualifications Wales. The Chemistry page (3410QS) carries identical wording, which confirms this is a family-wide amendment and not a Biology-specific problem.

VERDICT: The AMBER claim is REFUTED for the 2027 cohort. The amendment is real, but it applies to a different cohort. WJEC Biology 3400QS should be GREEN for 2027.

WHAT IS TRUE. WJEC did amend the specification. WJEC published Version 3 in February 2026. WJEC changed Unit 3 only. The current Unit 3 is "PRACTICAL ASSESSMENT", 30 marks. The new Unit 3 is "SCIENTIFIC ENQUIRY", 28 marks, with one enquiry from a choice of two, a 1-hour practical task (6 marks) and a 1-hour written task (22 marks). WJEC also added Appendix A "Scientific Enquiry Skills Framework" and changed the assessment objective weightings.

WHY IT DOES NOT HIT 2027. The updated specification states the cohort boundary three times:
1. Cover page: "For teaching from 2016 (with a new Unit 3 for first teaching from 2026). For award from 2018 (with a new Unit 3 award from 2028)."
2. Summary of Assessment: "It will be awarded for the first time in Summer 2018 (please note that the new Unit 3 will be awarded from 2028)."
3. Technical Information 4.1: "The original Unit 3 available in 2018 has been replaced by a new Unit 3 which will be available in 2028 (and each year thereafter) ... with the new Unit 3 awarded for the first time in Summer 2028."
The new Unit 3 is not available before 2028. The summer 2027 series uses the original Unit 3. WJEC also publishes both PDFs side by side, labelled "current version (not for teaching from September 2026)" and "updated version (for teaching from September 2026)". The 2027 cohort started Year 10 in September 2025, so it sits under the current version.

INDEPENDENT CONTENT CHECK. I downloaded both PDFs and diffed the Unit 1 and Unit 2 subject content (about 49,000 characters). Similarity was 0.9997. Only two differences appeared: a missing space ("(iron),vitamins" to "(iron), vitamins") and a pi symbol extraction artefact. Units 1 and 2 are substantively identical. That part of the claim is correct, and it is why the change is content-neutral for our lessons, which are built from Unit 1 and Unit 2. Unit 3 is a 10% centre-run NEA, not article content.

THE QUALIFICATION IS NOT WITHDRAWN. QiW record C00/0779/8 shows "WJEC Level 1/Level 2 GCSE in Biology" as eligible for publicly funded programmes for under-19s, with no withdrawal notice. The specification itself proves the qualification runs past 2027, because it schedules a new Unit 3 award for 2028. Chemistry 3410QS (C00/0779/9) carries the identical banner, so the same finding applies.

CONTRAST THAT SHOWS THE AUDIT MISFIRED. A genuine 2027 cliff-edge does exist, but on a different qualification. Legacy GCSE Science (Double Award) 3430QD states: "Summer 2027 will be the final full assessment opportunity for this qualification. A resit opportunity for examinations will be available in January 2028, subject to demand", and "From September 2026, learners must not be entered onto this qualification in Year 10". Separate Biology 3400QS carries no such notice. The AMBER flag looks like a bleed-over from the Double Award.

UNVERIFIED PARTS OF THE CLAIM. The survey details ("1-17 October 2025", "438 respondents", "60% of Welsh schools", "Option 1") are NOT published on the WJEC Biology or Chemistry pages. I could not confirm them. The WebSearch budget was exhausted, and qualificationswales.org returned an expired TLS certificate. The specification says only that "this amendment has been approved by Qualifications Wales". Treat those numbers as unsourced. The claim that the new Unit 3 aligns with "Unit 7: Scientific Enquiry" of the new GCSE The Sciences (Double Award) is only partly corroborated: WJEC's banner confirms content overview grids that map GCSE Biology topics into the new Double Award, and the new unit is indeed titled Scientific Enquiry, but I found no source naming it "Unit 7".

ACTION. Downgrade WJEC Biology 3400QS to GREEN for 2027. Flag one forward item: if we ever build for the September 2026 intake (2028 exams), use the updated specification, and rebuild any practical-skills revision guide against the new Scientific Enquiry Skills Framework. Impact stays small, because Unit 3 is 10% and is centre-assessed.

1. WJEC qualification page (English), spec code 3010CS. Explicit notice: "Summer 2026 will be the final full assessment opportunity for this qualification. A resit opportunity for examinations will be available in January 2027, subject to demand." The page also states learners must not be entered in Year 10 from September 2025.

2. WJEC qualification page (Welsh) carries the same notice independently. Translated: "Summer 2026 will be the last opportunity to assess this qualification in full. There will be an opportunity to resit the exams in January 2027, if there is demand for it."

3. Replacement qualification confirms the structure. WJEC GCSE Cymraeg Language and Literature, spec codes 3030QD (Double Award) and 3030QS (Single Award), first teaching September 2025. A two-year GCSE first taught in September 2025 is first assessed in summer 2027. This fills the exact slot 3010CS vacates, so the two dates are internally consistent rather than coincidental.

4. Regulator record. Made-for-Wales GCSEs are regulated by Qualifications Wales, not Ofqual — gov.uk's own "Find a regulated qualification" page directs users to QiW for Welsh qualifications. The QiW register shows WJEC Level 1/Level 2 GCSE in Welsh Literature / Llenyddiaeth Gymraeg, approval number C00/0720/9 (Ofqual QN 601/4914/0), status "No longer available to new learners". An older entry, C00/0236/2, is "No longer available". The two new Cymraeg Language and Literature entries, C00/4968/8 and C00/5087/0, are approved National Qualifications.

Ofqual corroborates but is not the governing authority here. Record 601/4914/0 reads "No longer awarded" with an operational end of 21 September 2015. That short window reflects Ofqual handing sole regulation to Qualifications Wales in 2015, not the qualification's real life. Treat it as supporting, not primary.

Important nuance for the ledger. A January 2027 resit exists, so the qualification does have an assessment opportunity inside calendar year 2027. It is not a summer 2027 opportunity, it is resit-only for candidates who already sat summer 2026, and it is conditional on demand. It cannot support a new 2027 teaching cohort. The first-pass verdict and its withdrawal_end_date wording are both accurate.

Method limitation, stated for transparency: the session WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200), so all evidence came from direct WebFetch and browser access to primary sources. This did not block the check — every required page was reached. The QiW register table renders via JavaScript, so I read it through the browser rather than WebFetch. Qualifications Wales' own policy site (qualificationswales.org) could not be fetched because its TLS certificate has expired; that source was not needed given the QiW register result.

action:
DO NOT BUILD GCSE Welsh Second Language (3020QS). It is withdrawn for the 2027 cohort. WJEC states on its own qualification page: "Summer 2026 will be the final full assessment opportunity for this qualification. A resit opportunity for examinations will be available in January 2027, subject to demand." It also states: "From September 2025, learners must not be entered onto this qualification in Year 10, they should be entered for GCSE Core Cymraeg - Teaching from 2025." A student sitting exams in summer 2027 started Year 10 in September 2025, so that student is on Core Cymraeg by rule. Content built against 3020QS would have zero addressable market from day one.

BUILD INSTEAD: GCSE Core Cymraeg, WJEC 3040CS. First teaching September 2025, first award summer 2027 (Unit 1 NEA runs November-December 2026, Unit 2 NEA February 2027, written exams summer 2027). This is a made-for-Wales qualification aligned to the Curriculum for Wales, so it is a genuine fresh build, not a re-skin of the Welsh Second Language spec.

CORRECT THE CATALOGUE. Our recorded code "3020CS" is a hybrid that matches no real WJEC qualification: 3020 is the legacy Welsh Second Language number, while the "CS" suffix belongs to Core Cymraeg (3040CS). Retire the welsh-second-language slug and re-catalogue as core-cymraeg / 3040CS. Two neighbouring codes are also worth adding to the Wales build plan: GCSE Cymraeg Language and Literature 3030QS (single) / 3030QD (double), also first teaching September 2025.

TIMING: the 2027 cohort is the very first Core Cymraeg cohort, so no past papers or examiner reports will exist until autumn 2027. Build from the spec plus WJEC sample assessment materials, and expect a revision pass once the first series is marked.

SOURCE CAVEAT: the Ofqual Register does not regulate this qualification, and the QiW (Qualifications in Wales) register serves its detail pages via JavaScript, so I could not machine-read the formal operational end date. The verdict rests on WJEC's own qualification page, which I fetched twice with consistent results, corroborated by Qualifications Wales confirming Core Cymraeg is live. The withdrawal statement is unambiguous, so confidence stays high.

verify.reasoning:
The first-pass RED verdict is correct. I tried to refute it and failed.

EVIDENCE ON THE BOARD'S OWN SITE (WJEC). The qualification page carries a notice. I fetched the page twice with different prompts. Both fetches returned the same three statements verbatim:
1. "Summer 2026 will be the final full assessment opportunity for this qualification."
2. "A resit opportunity for examinations will be available in January 2027, subject to demand."
3. "From September 2025, learners must not be entered onto this qualification in Year 10, they should be entered for GCSE Core Cymraeg - Teaching from 2025."

Statement 1 is an explicit final-assessment date before summer 2027. This meets the bar for confirmed_withdrawn.

Statement 3 is decisive for our purpose. A summer 2027 cohort starts Year 10 in September 2025. WJEC bars that exact cohort from entry. So no 2027 candidate can legitimately follow this specification.

Statement 2 gives a January 2027 resit series only, and only "subject to demand". A resit series is not a full assessment opportunity, and it is not summer 2027. It does not support a 2027 build.

SPEC CODE DISCREPANCY. The audit records 3020CS. The WJEC page shows entry code 3020QS, plus QWADN and Qualifications Wales approval number C00/1166/2. 3020CS is a sibling entry code inside the same 3020 Welsh Second Language family. It is the same specification and the same withdrawal. The discrepancy does not change the verdict.

REPLACEMENT. GCSE Core Cymraeg (teaching from 2025) replaces this qualification. WJEC names it directly in the notice.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED TO FIND CONTRARY EVIDENCE:
- Ofqual register: register.ofqual.gov.uk now redirects to find-a-qualification.services.ofqual.gov.uk, then to a generic gov.uk landing page. No qualification data was retrievable. This is expected and neutral. Welsh Second Language is a Wales-only qualification regulated by Qualifications Wales, not Ofqual, so an Ofqual listing would not exist regardless.
- QiW register (qiw.wales): the search is a JavaScript application. WebFetch returned the search shell only, with no qualification records. A direct detail URL for C00/1166/2 returned 404.
- Qualifications Wales news and reform pages: the URLs tried returned 404. I found no announcement of a delay, a deferral, or an extension of the legacy specification beyond summer 2026.
- WJEC key dates and entry codes pages: returned 404.

I found no source anywhere stating a summer 2027 assessment series for 3020.

CAVEAT ON METHOD. The WebSearch budget for this session was already exhausted (200 of 200 calls) before I started, so I could not run broad discovery searches. All work used direct WebFetch against known authoritative URLs. This limited my ability to find obscure contrary notices. However, the board's own qualification page is the primary authority, and it is unambiguous, so the limitation does not weaken the conclusion.

VERDICT. Do not build or offer WJEC Welsh Second Language 3020 for the 2027 cohort. If a Welsh-language build is wanted for 2027, build GCSE Core Cymraeg instead.

name: GCSE Computer Science

This is teaching-support clarification and extra practice material. It does not change the specification. (2) 6 July 2026 "Computer Science July Update" - results-day administration, multi-factor authentication, grade boundaries, examiner reports and professional-development events. No content change. Neither update mentions withdrawal, redevelopment, a new specification, or a change to the programming languages permitted for Paper 2. Note for future auditors: QN 601/8058/4 carries an Ofqual operational start date of 01 September 2016 because Pearson revised the specification under the SAME qualification number when it replaced the 2016 spec (1CP1) with the 2020 spec (1CP2). The old 1CP1 entry code is dead (last exams 2021); 1CP2 is the correct and only live code.
action: KEEP - no action needed for the 2027 cohort. Our content is current and fit. Three independent authorities agree. (1) Ofqual: QN 601/8058/4, "Pearson Edexcel Level 1/Level 2 GCSE (9-1) in Computer Science", status "Available to learners", with NO operational end date and NO certification end date. (2) Pearson: the "Pearson Edexcel GCSE Summer 2027 Examination Timetable - FINAL" lists both papers, 1CP2/01 (Paper 1: Principles of Computer Science) and 1CP2/02 (Paper 2: Application of Computational Thinking, onscreen). Summer 2027 exams are confirmed. (3) The Pearson qualification page shows no withdrawal, discontinuation, final-assessment or replacement notice. The accredited specification is locked at Issue 1 (January 2020) and predates our build by six years, so no re-build or content review is required. OPTIONAL, LOW PRIORITY (do not treat as a status trigger): the June 2026 update released "Getting Started Guide V4" with extra exemplification of specification scope, and Specimen Set 4 practice papers. Neither changes what students must know, but the Specimen Set 4 papers are a free source of fresh, exam-authentic practice questions if we ever refresh the Edexcel Computer Science question bank. Note also that the WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted, so this verdict rests entirely on direct fetches of primary sources; that is a stronger evidence base than search snippets, hence high confidence.

action: Keep as is — no content work needed. Summer 2027 is fully served: Pearson's official BTEC Tech Awards Key Dates Schedule 2026/2027 (version 1.0, March 2026) carries a complete May/June 2027 series — Pearson-set assignments released 07 Sep 2026, entry deadline 21 Feb 2027, first exam sitting 04 May 2027, results to learners 19 Aug 2027 — plus a December/January 2027 series. Last learner registration in England and Northern Ireland is 31 Aug 2030, so the qualification runs well past the 2027 cohort. There is no withdrawal, final-assessment or discontinuation notice on Pearson's page. The DfE level 3 BTEC defunding programme does NOT touch this pre-16 Level 1/2 Tech Award; do not confuse the two. One low-priority spot-check worth doing when convenient: confirm our lessons use "stroke" and not "cerebral vascular accident", since that is the tell for Issue 4 versus Issue 5 wording. A grep of the local repo found no stale instances, but our content lives in Supabase, so the repo check is not conclusive.
